name: SafetyCulture
description: Run inspections, manage actions, and resolve issues in SafetyCulture

authentication.name: API Token
authentication.description: Authenticate with a SafetyCulture API token.

setupGuide.title: Create a SafetyCulture API token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a SafetyCulture account with API access. For shared production integrations, SafetyCulture recommends using a service user token instead of a personal user token.

steps.title: Create a service user token (recommended)
steps.description: Follow SafetyCulture's official service-user guide to create a service user, assign the right permissions, and generate its API token.

steps.title: Use a personal API token only if you do not manage service users
steps.description: If this connection should mirror your own account access, follow SafetyCulture's official user-token guide and generate a personal API token from the web app.

steps.title: Paste the token into MindCloud
steps.description: When MindCloud asks for the API Key value, paste the token you copied from SafetyCulture and save the connection.

name: SalesDrive
description: SalesDrive is a Ukrainian CRM for online stores and sales teams, with API coverage for orders, products, payments, documents, calls, delivery/payment metadata, and currency rates.

authentication.name: SalesDrive API Keys
authentication.description: Connect SalesDrive with the account subdomain, Database API Key, and Account API Key.
authentication.notes: SalesDrive uses two API keys for one account. Order, form, catalog, currency, field, delivery, payment-method, and status endpoints use the Database/Form API Key sent as `Form-Api-Key`. Payment and document-list endpoints use the Account API Key sent as `Account-Api-Key`. Configure both keys in the same connection for full action coverage.

credentials.name: Account Subdomain
credentials.description: The SalesDrive account subdomain only, for example `demo` from `https://demo.salesdrive.me`.

credentials.name: Account API Key
credentials.description: SalesDrive Account API Key for payment and document-list APIs. This is separate from the Database API Key stored in the standard API Key field.

setupGuide.title: Connect SalesDrive
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need the SalesDrive account subdomain plus two API keys: the Database API Key and the Account API Key.

steps.title: Copy the account subdomain
steps.description: Open your SalesDrive workspace and copy only the subdomain before `.salesdrive.me`. Do not include `https://` or `.salesdrive.me`.

steps.title: Copy the Database API Key
steps.description: In SalesDrive settings, open the API/API keys area and copy the Database API Key used for order, form, catalog, currency, field, delivery, payment-method, and status APIs. Paste it into the API Key field.

steps.title: Copy the Account API Key
steps.description: From the same SalesDrive API key area, copy the Account API Key used for payment and document-list APIs. Paste it into the Account API Key field.

steps.title: Save and test the connection
steps.description: Save the connection. The connection test verifies the account subdomain and Database API Key with the order-status API. Payment and document actions also require the Account API Key.

steps.title: Save and test the connection

authentication.notes: Use the raw SalesRender API token. SalesRender expects the token in the `Authorization` header without a `Bearer ` prefix. The `companyId` used in requests must match the SalesRender company that issued the token.

arguments.description: Specify a delay in milliseconds before fetching the content, allowing the page sufficient time to load.

arguments.name: Timeout
arguments.description: Timeout in milliseconds for the request

arguments.name: Session Name
arguments.description: Set a name for your session to facilitate searching and viewing in the historical session list.

arguments.name: Session TTL
arguments.description: Controls the session duration and automatically closes the browser instance after timeout. Measured in seconds (s), defaults to 180 seconds (3 minutes), customizable between 60 seconds (1 minute) and 900 seconds (recommended maximum 15 minutes, but longer times can be set). Once the specified TTL is reached, the session will expire and Scraping Browser will close the browser instance to free resources.

arguments.name: Session Recording
arguments.description: Whether to enable session recording. When enabled, the entire browser session execution process will be automatically recorded, and after the session is completed, it can be replayed and viewed in the historical session list details. Defaults to false.

arguments.name: Proxy Country
arguments.description: Sets the target country/region for the proxy, sending requests via an IP address from that region. You can specify a country code (e.g., US for the United States, GB for the United Kingdom, ANY for any country). See country codes for all supported options.

arguments.name: Proxy URL
arguments.description:
Used to set the browser’s proxy URL, for example: http://user:pass@ip:port. If this parameter is set, all other proxy_* parameters will be ignored.

- 💡Custom proxy functionality is currently only available to Enterprise and Enterprise Enhanced subscription users Upgrade Now
- 💡Enterprise-level custom users can contact us to use custom proxies.

arguments.name: Fingerprint
arguments.description: A browser fingerprint is a nearly unique “digital fingerprint” created using your browser and device configuration information, which can be used to track your online activity even without cookies. Fortunately, configuring fingerprints in Scraping Browser is optional. We offer deep customization of browser fingerprints, such as core parameters like browser user agent, time zone, language, and screen resolution, and support extending functionality through custom launch parameters. Suitable for multi-account management, data collection, and privacy protection scenarios, using scrapeless’s own Chromium browser completely avoids detection. By default, our Scraping Browser service generates a random fingerprint for each session. Reference

actions.name: Create Browser Session Task
actions.description: Creates a browser session task in Scrapeless.

arguments.name: Session TTL
arguments.description: The session_ttl parameter controls the duration of the session and automatically closes the browser instance after the session times out. The unit of session_ttl is seconds (S), with a default value of 180 seconds (i.e., 3 minutes), and can be customized between 60 seconds (1 minute) and 900 seconds (15 minutes). When the specified TTL time is reached, the session will become invalid, and Scraping Browser will close the browser instance to release resources. Please set the session_ttl reasonably according to the task requirements to ensure that the operations are completed before the session times out.

arguments.name: Proxy URL
arguments.description:

> 💡Custom proxy functionality is currently only available to subscribers. [Upgrade here](https://www.scrapeless.com/en/pricing)

arguments.name: Proxy Country
arguments.description: The proxyCountry parameter is used to set the target country of the proxy, making the request sent through the IP address of that region. You can customize the proxy source by specifying a country code for proxyCountry (e.g., US for the United States, GB for the United Kingdom, ANY for any country). Scraping Browser will provide the corresponding IP address based on the specified country, which helps meet regional access restrictions or geographic positioning needs. Required if `proxyURL` not set.

arguments.name: Proxy State
arguments.description: Specifies the target state/province within the selected country for more granular proxy routing. Must be used in conjunction with `proxyCountry`. Accepts state codes (e.g., `CA` for California, `NY` for New York). Available for select countries with defined state/province divisions. [learn mor](https://docs.scrapeless.com/en/proxies/features/proxy)

arguments.name: Proxy City
arguments.description: Specifies the target city within the selected state/province for city-level proxy routing. Must be used in conjunction with `proxyCountry` and `proxyState`. Provides the most precise geographic targeting. Availability depends on proxy infrastructure in specific cities.

actions.name: Create Crawl Job
actions.description: Creates a new crawl job in Scrapeless.

arguments.name: Url
arguments.description: The base URL to start crawling from

arguments.name: Limit
arguments.description: Maximum number of pages to crawl. Default limit is 10000.

arguments.name: Exclude Paths
arguments.description: URL pathname regex patterns that exclude matching URLs from the crawl. For example, if you set "excludePaths": ["blog/.*"] for the base URL firecrawl.dev, any results matching that pattern will be excluded, such as https://www.scrapeless.com/blog/firecrawl-launch-week-1-recap.

arguments.name: Include Paths
arguments.description: URL pathname regex patterns that include matching URLs in the crawl. Only the paths that match the specified patterns will be included in the response. For example, if you set "includePaths": ["blog/.*"] for the base URL firecrawl.dev, only results matching that pattern will be included, such as https://www.scrapeless.com/blog/firecrawl-launch-week-1-recap.

arguments.name: Max Depth
arguments.description: Maximum depth to crawl relative to the base URL. Basically, the max number of slashes the pathname of a scraped URL may contain.

arguments.name: Max Discovery Depth
arguments.description: Maximum depth to crawl based on discovery order. The root site and sitemapped pages has a discovery depth of 0. For example, if you set it to 1, and you set ignoreSitemap, you will only crawl the entered URL and all URLs that are linked on that page.

arguments.name: Ignore Sitemap
arguments.description: Ignore the website sitemap when crawling

arguments.name: Ignore Query Parameters
arguments.description: Do not re-scrape the same path with different (or none) query parameters

arguments.name: Deduplicate Similar URLs
arguments.description: Controls whether similar URLs should be deduplicated.

arguments.name: Regex On Full URL
arguments.description: Controls whether the regular expression should be applied to the full URL.

arguments.name: Allow Backward Links
arguments.description: By default, the crawl skips sublinks that aren’t part of the URL hierarchy you specify. For example, crawling https://example.com/products/ wouldn’t capture pages under https://example.com/promotions/deal-567. To include such links, enable the `allowBackwardLinks` parameter.

arguments.name: Allow External Links
arguments.description: Allows the crawler to follow links to external websites.

arguments.name: Delay
arguments.description: Delay in seconds between scrapes. This helps respect website rate limits.

arguments.name: Formats
arguments.description: Formats to include in the output.

arguments.name: Only Main Content
arguments.description: Only return the main content of the page excluding headers, navs, footers, etc.

arguments.name: Include Tags
arguments.description: Tags to include in the output.

arguments.name: Exclude Tags
arguments.description: Tags to exclude from the output.

arguments.name: Fingerprint
arguments.description: A browser fingerprint is a nearly unique “digital fingerprint” created using your browser and device configuration information, which can be used to track your online activity even without cookies. Fortunately, configuring fingerprints in Scraping Browser is optional. We offer deep customization of browser fingerprints, such as core parameters like browser user agent, time zone, language, and screen resolution, and support extending functionality through custom launch parameters. setupGuide.title: Connect SEA-LION API
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a SEA-LION Playground account and an API key from the SEA-LION API Key Manager.

steps.title: Sign in to SEA-LION Playground
steps.description: Open the SEA-LION Playground and sign in with your Google account.

steps.title: Open API Key Manager
steps.description: From the dashboard, open API Key on the side menu or use Launch Key Manager on the home dashboard.

steps.title: Create a trial API key
steps.description: Click Create New Trial API Key, enter a name, and generate the key you want MindCloud to use.

name: Seam
description: Universal API for smart locks, access systems, thermostats, noise sensors, and related access-control workflows through Seam.

setupGuide.title: Create a Seam API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the Seam Console workspace you want to use with MindCloud.

steps.title: Open Seam Console
steps.description: Open the Seam Console and choose the workspace you want this connection to use.

steps.title: Go to API Keys
steps.description: In the left navigation pane, click API Keys for the selected workspace.

steps.title: Create a new API key
steps.description: Click Add API Key, enter a name for the key, and create it.

steps.title: Copy the API key
steps.description: Copy the new key immediately and store it somewhere secure. You will paste this value into the MindCloud connection form.

steps.title: Test the key with Get Workspace
steps.description: After saving the connection in MindCloud, run the Seam Get Workspace action to confirm the key works.

setupGuide.title: Connect SeaTable with an API token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the SeaTable base you want this connection to control. SeaTable base operations require a short-lived Base Token and the Base UUID in addition to your long-lived API token.

steps.title: Create or copy a SeaTable API token for your base
steps.description: In SeaTable Cloud, create an API token for the specific base you want to use. Give it the permission level this wrapper needs.

steps.title: Generate a Base Token from that API token
steps.description: Use SeaTable's documented Get Base-Token with API-Token endpoint to exchange your API token for a temporary Base Token.

steps.title: Copy the values into this MindCloud connection
steps.description: Paste your long-lived API token into the API key field. Paste the returned access_token into Base Token and the returned dtable_uuid into Base UUID.

name: Sentry IO
description: Monitor Sentry organizations, projects, issues, events, teams, releases, replays, and Explore data from MindCloud workflows and Cirra.

authentication.name: Sentry OAuth2
authentication.description: Connect to Sentry using OAuth2 authorization code flow.
authentication.notes: Sentry OAuth2 uses authorization-code flow. PKCE is disabled in this MindCloud draft because the current OAuth URL builder emits lowercase s256 for code_challenge_method, while Sentry requires uppercase S256. Register this exact redirect URI in the Sentry OAuth application: https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/sentryIO/callback. Requested scopes are limited to documented Sentry scopes: org:read project:read team:read member:read event:read event:write project:releases. Access tokens are sent with Authorization: Bearer. Refresh token requests are form-encoded body requests with client_id, client_secret, grant_type=refresh_token, and refresh_token; the blank Authorization refresh header is intentional to prevent the runtime from auto-adding Basic auth, which Sentry's documented refresh example does not use.
authentication.scopes: org:read project:read team:read member:read event:read event:write project:releases

description: ServiceTitan is a cloud-based software platform for home and commercial service businesses that manages customers, jobs, scheduling, dispatching, invoicing, payments, and other field service operations.

authentication.description: Temporary custom auth.

setupGuide.title: Connect your ServiceTitan account
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Use a ServiceTitan account with Generate API Application Key and Manage API Application Access permissions. Ask your administrator to enable them if needed.

glossary.definition: The ServiceTitan account whose data you want to connect.
The permissions that control which data an application can read or change.
The application's external-data identifier, separate from its App Key.

steps.title: Choose your environment
steps.description: For your live ServiceTitan account, leave Development Environment off in the connection form. Turn it on only when connecting a ServiceTitan integration environment used for testing. Obtain credentials from the environment you intend to connect.

steps.title: Find your Tenant
steps.description: In ServiceTitan, open Settings, then Integrations > API Application Access. Copy Your Tenant ID into Tenant in the connection form.

steps.title: Open or create your application
steps.description: Sign in to the developer portal using the Production Environment User or Integration Environment User option that matches your account. Open your application in My Apps. If creating one, choose +New App, fill in its details, add your Tenant ID under Tenant(s), and select the API scopes needed for your integration.

steps.title: Fill in App Key
steps.description: In the application's Keys > Application Key section, copy the key and paste it into App Key in the connection form.

steps.title: Fill in App GUID when using external data
steps.description: If your application has an External Data Application GUID configured under App Details, enter that same value in App GUID in the connection form.

steps.title: Allow the application to access your account
steps.description: Return to ServiceTitan's API Application Access page. Click Connect New App, select your application, and click Connect. Review the requested permissions and click Allow Access if they are correct. If the application is missing, check that its developer has added your Tenant ID.

steps.title: Fill in Client ID and Client Secret
steps.description: In the connected application's Application Details, copy Client ID into Client ID in the connection form. Under Client Secret, click Generate and paste the resulting value into Client Secret. Keep the secret private.

name: ServiceTrade
description: Field service management platform for commercial contractors. ServiceTrade manages locations, assets, appointments, jobs, service requests, quotes, invoices, users, and webhooks.

authentication.name: OAuth2 Client Credentials
authentication.description: Legacy OAuth2 client-credentials auth retained only for internal migration fallback; end users should connect with ServiceTrade username and password instead.

credentials.name: Client Secret
credentials.description: The ServiceTrade OAuth2 client_secret value for your tenant.

credentials.name: Client ID
credentials.description: The ServiceTrade OAuth2 client_id value for your tenant.

setupGuide.title: Set up ServiceTrade OAuth2 client credentials
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a ServiceTrade account with API access. If you do not already have OAuth2 credentials, create them from the ServiceTrade API using an authenticated ServiceTrade account.

steps.title: Create OAuth2 credentials
steps.description: Using an authenticated ServiceTrade account, call POST https://api.servicetrade.com/api/oauth2/credentials and copy the client_id and client_secret values returned by ServiceTrade.

steps.title: Enter the client credentials in MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the ServiceTrade client ID and client secret into the connection form. MindCloud will exchange them for bearer tokens automatically.

steps.title: Test the connection
steps.description: Run the connection test. MindCloud will request an access token from POST /api/oauth2/token and validate it against GET /api/oauth2/userinfo.

actions.name: Send SMS
actions.description: Creates a new SMS in Seven.

arguments.name: To
arguments.description:
Recipient number of the SMS. This can also be the name of a contact or a group.
Our API accepts all common formats such as 0049171999999999 , 49171999999999 , +49171999999999 .
Multiple recipients are
transferred comma-separated. Ideally, you should enter the phone number in international format after
 E.164 .

arguments.name: From
arguments.description: Sender of the SMS. This may contain a maximum of 11 alphanumeric or 16 numeric characters.

arguments.name: Delay
arguments.description:
Date/time for delayed sending. Optionally Unix timestamp or a timestamp in the format YYYY-MM-DD
hh:mm:ss.

arguments.name: Flash
arguments.description:
Send SMS as Flash SMS. These are shown directly on the recipient's display. On most devices, no sender
is displayed for Flash SMS, with the exception of some older models.

arguments.name: Udh
arguments.description:
Individual User Data Header (UDH) of the SMS. If specified and variable text contains hex code, the
message is sent as an 8-bit binary SMS. 050003CC0201 (concatenated message: reference number 204, part 1
of 2)

arguments.name: Ttl
arguments.description:
Specifies the validity period of the SMS in minutes. The default is 2880, i.e. 48 hours. Please note
that not all networks allow a different setting.

arguments.name: Label
arguments.description:
Optionally set a separate label for each SMS so that you can assign it to your statistics. Max. 100
characters, permitted characters: a-z, A-Z, 0-9, .-_@.

arguments.name: Performance Tracking
arguments.description:
Activate click and performance tracking for URLs found in the SMS text. This also activates the URL
shortener.

arguments.name: Foreign Id
arguments.description:
Enter your own ID for this message. You will receive the foreign_id in turn for callbacks for status
reports etc. Max. 64 characters, permitted characters: a-z, A-Z, 0-9, .-_@.

arguments.name: Is Binary
arguments.description: If true , the SMS will be sent as binary data.

arguments.name: Get Replies
arguments.description: Activates the reply function. Replies are assigned for 48 hours. The sender is automatically overwritten.

setupGuide.title: Get your Shippo API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Use a Shippo test token while you configure and test this connection. Switch to a live token only when you are ready to create real labels and charges.

steps.description: Open Shippo sign up, create your account, and finish the registration prompts.

steps.title: Sign in to the Shippo API portal
steps.description: Log in with your Shippo credentials so you can manage API credentials.

steps.title: Open Developer keys
steps.description: In the API Configuration menu, select Developer keys.

steps.title: Create a test key for setup
steps.description: Click Create new test key and copy the generated value. Shippo says test keys begin with shippo_test_. Use a live key only when you are ready for production usage.

steps.title: Paste the key into your MindCloud connection
steps.description: Return to MindCloud and paste the copied Shippo key into the API Key field for this connection.

name: ShipWise
description: ShipWise provides shipping, order, rate, label, tracking, packaging, carrier-service, and marketplace/channel API workflows for high-volume shipping operations.

authentication.name: API Token
authentication.description: Use a ShipWise API token as a Bearer token in the Authorization header.
authentication.notes: ShipWise uses API-key style Bearer authentication: `Authorization: Bearer {token}`. Use production base URL `https://api.shipwise.com/`; test environments use `https://testapi.shipwise.com/`.

setupGuide.title: Connect ShipWise
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to a ShipWise account that can create API tokens.

steps.title: Open the API settings in ShipWise
steps.description: In ShipWise, navigate to Settings and select API.

steps.title: Create a token
steps.description: Click Create Token, select the call types this connection needs, enter a token name, and create the token.

steps.title: Copy the token
steps.description: After the token is created, click Copy Token and paste it into the API key field for this connection.

actions.name: Activate Inventory Item
actions.description: Activates an inventory item in Shopify.

arguments.name: API Version
arguments.description:
e.g. `2026-01`

As of version 2026-01, this mutation supports an optional idempotency key using the @idempotent directive. As of version 2026-04, the idempotency key is required and must be provided using the @idempotent directive. For more information, see the idempotency documentation.

arguments.name: Inventory Item ID
arguments.description: The ID of the location of the inventory item being activated.

arguments.name: Query
arguments.description:
This mutation __Activates an inventory item at a location with idempotency enabled__

To see all available examples [see the documentation](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/latest/mutations/inventoryActivate?example=activate-an-inventory-item-at-a-location-with-idempotency-enabled-2026-01-onwards)

arguments.name: Location ID

arguments.name: API Version
arguments.description:

arguments.name: Inventory Item ID
arguments.description: The ID of the location of the inventory item being activated.

arguments.name: Query
arguments.description:
This mutation __Activates an inventory item at a location with idempotency enabled__

To see all available examples [see the documentation](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/latest/mutations/inventoryActivate?example=activate-an-inventory-item-at-a-location-with-idempotency-enabled-2026-01-onwards)
arguments.defaultValue: mutation InventoryActivate(   $inventoryItemId: ID!,    $locationId: ID! ) {   inventoryActivate(     inventoryItemId: $inventoryItemId,      locationId: $locationId   ) {     inventoryLevel {       id       canDeactivate       createdAt       item {         id       }       location {         id       }       quantities(names: ["available"]) {         name         quantity       }       updatedAt     }   } }

arguments.description: Randomness setting. Float value between 0.0 and 1.5. Closer to 0 will make the output less random.

arguments.description: Randomness setting. Alternative to `temperature`. Float value between 0.0 and 1.0. Closer to 0 will make the output less random.

arguments.name: Confidence
arguments.description:
Threshold to fire a speech-detect event at the end of the utterance. Float value between 0.0 and 1.0.
Decreasing this value will reduce the pause after the user speaks, but may introduce false positives.

arguments.name: Presence Penalty
arguments.description: Aversion to staying on topic. Float value between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values increase the model's likelihood to talk about new topics.

arguments.name: Frequency Penalty
arguments.description: Aversion to repeating lines. Float value between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values decrease the model's likelihood to repeat the same line verbatim.

arguments.name: Steps
arguments.description: An array of objects that define the steps in the context. These steps are used to define the flow of the conversation.

arguments.name: Presence Penalty

arguments.name: Frequency Penalty
arguments.description: Aversion to repeating lines. Float value between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values decrease the model's likelihood to repeat the same line verbatim.

arguments.name: Acknowledge Interruptions
arguments.description: Instructs the agent to acknowledge crosstalk and confirm user input when the user speaks over the agent.

arguments.name: AI Name
arguments.description: Sets the name the AI agent responds to for wake/activation purposes. When using `enable_pause`, `start_paused`, or `speak_when_spoken_to`, the user must say this name to get the agent's attention.

arguments.name: AI Volume
arguments.description: Adjust the volume of the AI. Allowed values from `-50` - `50`.

arguments.name: App Name
arguments.description: A custom identifier for the AI application instance. This name is included in webhook payloads.

arguments.name: Attention Timeout
arguments.description: Amount of time, in ms, to wait before prompting the user to respond. Allowed values from `10,000` - `600,000`. Set to `0` to disable.

arguments.name: Attention Timeout Prompt
arguments.description: A custom prompt that is fed into the AI when the attention_timeout is reached.

arguments.name: Background File
arguments.description: URL of audio file to play in the background while AI plays in foreground.

arguments.name: Background File Loops
arguments.description: Maximum number of times to loop playing the background file. `undefined` means loop indefinitely.

arguments.name: Background File Volume
arguments.description: Defines background_file volume within a range of `-50` to `50`.

arguments.name: Barge Match String
arguments.description:
Takes a string, including a regular expression, defining barge behavior.
For example, this param can direct the AI to stop when the word 'hippopotomus' is input.

arguments.name: Barge Min Words
arguments.description: Defines the number of words that must be input before triggering barge behavior, in a range of `1-99`.

arguments.name: Conscience
arguments.description: Sets the prompt which binds the agent to its purpose.

arguments.name: Convo
arguments.description: Injects pre-existing conversation history into the AI session at startup. This allows you to seed the AI agent with context from a previous conversation or provide example interactions.

arguments.name: Convo
arguments.description: Injects pre-existing conversation history into the AI session at startup. This allows you to seed the AI agent with context from a previous conversation or provide example interactions.

arguments.name: Conversation Id
arguments.description: Used by `check_for_input` and `save_conversation` to identify an individual conversation.

arguments.name: Debug Webhook Level
arguments.description: Enables debugging to the set URL. Allowed values from `0` - `1`.

arguments.name: Debug Webhook Url
arguments.description: Each interaction between the AI and end user is posted in real time to the established URL.

arguments.name: Debug
arguments.description: Enables debug mode for the AI session.

arguments.name: Direction
arguments.description: Forces the direction of the call to the assistant. Valid values are `inbound` and `outbound`.

arguments.name: Direction
arguments.description: Forces the direction of the call to the assistant. Valid values are `inbound` and `outbound`.

arguments.name: Digit Termiantors
arguments.description: DTMF digit, as a string, to signal the end of input (ex: '#')

arguments.name: Digit Timeout
arguments.description: Time, in ms, at the end of digit input to detect end of input. Allowed values from `250` - `10,000`.

arguments.name: End Of Speech Timeout
arguments.description: Amount of silence, in ms, at the end of an utterance to detect end of speech. Allowed values from `250` - `10,000`.

arguments.name: Enable Inner Dialog
arguments.description: Enables the inner dialog feature for background conversation analysis.

arguments.name: Enable Pause
arguments.description: Enables the pause/resume functionality for the AI agent.

arguments.name: Enable Turn Detection
arguments.description: Enables intelligent turn detection that monitors partial speech transcripts.

arguments.name: Eleven Labs Stability
arguments.description: The stability slider determines how stable the voice is and the randomness between each generation. Lowering this slider introduces a broader emotional range for the voice.

arguments.name: Eleven Labs Similarity
arguments.description: The similarity slider dictates how closely the AI should adhere to the original voice when attempting to replicate it. The higher the similarity, the closer the AI will sound to the original voice.

arguments.name: Energy Level
arguments.description: Amount of energy necessary for bot to hear you (in dB). Allowed values from `0.0` - `100.0`.

arguments.name: Hold Music
arguments.description: A URL for the hold music to play, accepting WAV, mp3, and FreeSWITCH tone_stream.

arguments.name: Hold On Process
arguments.description: Enables hold music during SWAIG processing.

arguments.name: Inactivity Timeout
arguments.description: Amount of time, in ms, to wait before exiting the app due to inactivity. Allowed values from `10,000` - `3,600,000`.

arguments.name: Inner Dialog Model
arguments.description: Specifies the AI model to use for the inner dialog feature.

arguments.name: Inner Dialog Prompt
arguments.description: The system prompt that guides the inner dialog AI's behavior.

arguments.name: Inner Dialog Synced
arguments.description: When enabled, synchronizes the inner dialog with the main conversation flow.

arguments.name: Input Poll Freq
arguments.description:
Check for input function with check_for_input.
Example use case: Feeding an inbound SMS to AI on a voice call, eg., for collecting an email address or other complex information.

arguments.name: Interrupt On Noise
arguments.description: When enabled, barges agent upon any sound interruption longer than 1 second.

arguments.name: Interrupt Prompt
arguments.description: Provide a prompt for the agent to handle crosstalk.

arguments.name: Local Tz
arguments.description: The local timezone setting for the AI. Value should use `IANA TZ ID`

arguments.name: Max Response Tokens
arguments.description: Sets the maximum number of tokens the AI model can generate in a single response.

arguments.name: Outbound Attention Timeout
arguments.description: Sets a time duration for the outbound call recipient to respond to the AI agent before timeout, in a range from `10000` to `600000`.

arguments.name: Persist Global Data
arguments.description: When enabled, global_data persists across multiple AI agent invocations within the same call.

arguments.name: Pom Format
arguments.description: Specifies the output format for structured prompts. Valid values are `markdown` or `xml`.

arguments.name: Save Conversation
arguments.description:
Send a summary of the conversation after the call ends.
This requires a `post_url` to be set in the ai parameters and the `conversation_id` defined below.
This eliminates the need for a `post_prompt` in the ai parameters.

arguments.name: Speak When Spoken To
arguments.description: When enabled, the AI agent remains silent until directly addressed by name.

arguments.name: Start Paused
arguments.description: When enabled, the AI agent starts in a paused state.

arguments.name: Swaig Allow Settings
arguments.description: Allows tweaking any of the indicated settings, such as `barge_match_string`, using the returned SWML from the SWAIG function.

arguments.name: Swaig Allow Swml
arguments.description: Allows your SWAIG to return SWML to be executed.

arguments.name: Swaig Post Conversation
arguments.description: Post entire conversation to any SWAIG call.

arguments.name: Swaig Post Swml Vars
arguments.description: Controls whether SWML variables are included in SWAIG function webhook payloads.

arguments.name: Transfer Summary
arguments.description: Pass a summary of a conversation from one AI agent to another. For example, transfer a call summary between support agents in two departments.

arguments.name: Turn Detection Timeout
arguments.description: Time in milliseconds to wait after detecting a potential end-of-turn before finalizing speech recognition.

arguments.name: Vad Config
arguments.description: Configures Silero Voice Activity Detection (VAD) settings. Format: `threshold` or `threshold:frame_ms`. The threshold (0-100) sets sensitivity for detecting voice activity. The optional frame_ms (16-40) sets frame duration in milliseconds.

arguments.name: Wait For User
arguments.description: When false, AI agent will initialize dialogue after call is setup. When true, agent will wait for the user to speak first.

arguments.name: Wake Prefix
arguments.description: Specifies an additional prefix that must be spoken along with the agent's name to wake the agent.

arguments.name: Pronounce
arguments.description: An array of JSON objects to clarify the AI's pronunciation of words or expressions.

arguments.name: Hints
arguments.description: An array of hints (as strings) to provide context to the dialogue.

arguments.name: Languages
arguments.description: An array of JSON objects defining supported languages in the conversation.

arguments.name: Web Hook Url
arguments.description: Default URL to send status callbacks and reports to. Authentication can also be set in the url in the format of `username:password@url.`

arguments.name: Native Functions
arguments.description: Prebuilt functions the AI agent is able to call from this list of available native functions

arguments.name: Includes

arguments.name: Call Handler
arguments.description:
Specify how the SIP endpoint will handle outbound calls.
- **default**: The SIP endpoint will pull the outbound policy setting from the [SIP Profile Settings](https://my.signalwire.com?page=sip_profile/edit). This allows centralized management of outbound call behavior across multiple endpoints from a single configuration.
- **passthrough**: The SIP endpoint will be allowed to dial PSTN numbers. This permits outbound calling to traditional phone numbers without restrictions.
- **block-pstn**: The SIP endpoint will be blocked from dialing PSTN numbers. Use this to restrict the endpoint from initiating calls to the public telephone network.
- **resource**: Outbound calls from this SIP endpoint will dial the specified resource and execute its instructions. Requires setting `calling_handler_resource_id` to a valid resource. This enables custom call handling workflows for outbound calls. See the [Fabric REST API](/rest/signalwire-rest/endpoints/fabric) for valid resource types.

- **default**: The SIP endpoint will pull the outbound policy setting from the [SIP Profile Settings](https://my.signalwire.com?page=sip_profile/edit). This allows centralized management of outbound call behavior across multiple endpoints from a single configuration.
- **passthrough**: The SIP endpoint will be allowed to dial PSTN numbers. This permits outbound calling to traditional phone numbers without restrictions.
- **block-pstn**: The SIP endpoint will be blocked from dialing PSTN numbers. Use this to restrict the endpoint from initiating calls to the public telephone network.
- **resource**: Outbound calls from this SIP endpoint will dial the specified resource and execute its instructions. Requires setting `calling_handler_resource_id` to a valid resource. This enables custom call handling workflows for outbound calls. See the [Fabric REST API](/rest/signalwire-rest/endpoints/fabric) for valid resource types.

actions.name: Update AI Agent
actions.description: Updates an existing AI agent in SignalWire.

arguments.name: Id
arguments.description: Unique ID of an AI Agent.

arguments.description: Unique ID of an AI Agent.

arguments.name: Text
arguments.description: The instructions to send to the agent.

arguments.name: Temperature
arguments.description: Randomness setting. Float value between 0.0 and 1.5. Closer to 0 will make the output less random.

arguments.name: Top P
arguments.description: Randomness setting. Alternative to `temperature`. Float value between 0.0 and 1.0. Closer to 0 will make the output less random.

arguments.name: Confidence
arguments.description:
Threshold to fire a speech-detect event at the end of the utterance. Float value between 0.0 and 1.0.
Decreasing this value will reduce the pause after the user speaks, but may introduce false positives.

arguments.name: Presence Penalty
arguments.description: Aversion to staying on topic. Float value between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values increase the model's likelihood to talk about new topics.

arguments.name: Frequency Penalty
arguments.description: Aversion to repeating lines. Float value between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values decrease the model's likelihood to repeat the same line verbatim.

arguments.name: Steps
arguments.description: An array of objects that define the steps in the context. These steps are used to define the flow of the conversation.

arguments.name: Frequency Penalty
arguments.description: Aversion to repeating lines. Float value between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values decrease the model's likelihood to repeat the same line verbatim.

arguments.name: Acknowledge Interruptions
arguments.description: Instructs the agent to acknowledge crosstalk and confirm user input when the user speaks over the agent.

arguments.name: AI Name
arguments.description: Sets the name the AI agent responds to for wake/activation purposes. When using `enable_pause`, `start_paused`, or `speak_when_spoken_to`, the user must say this name to get the agent's attention.

arguments.name: AI Volume
arguments.description: Adjust the volume of the AI. Allowed values from `-50` - `50`.

arguments.name: App Name
arguments.description: A custom identifier for the AI application instance. This name is included in webhook payloads.

arguments.name: Attention Timeout
arguments.description: Amount of time, in ms, to wait before prompting the user to respond. Allowed values from `10,000` - `600,000`. Set to `0` to disable.

arguments.name: Attention Timeout Prompt
arguments.description: A custom prompt that is fed into the AI when the attention_timeout is reached.

arguments.name: Background File
arguments.description: URL of audio file to play in the background while AI plays in foreground.

arguments.name: Background File Loops
arguments.description: Maximum number of times to loop playing the background file. `undefined` means loop indefinitely.

arguments.name: Background File Volume
arguments.description: Defines background_file volume within a range of `-50` to `50`.

arguments.name: Barge Match String
arguments.description:
Takes a string, including a regular expression, defining barge behavior.
For example, this param can direct the AI to stop when the word 'hippopotomus' is input.

arguments.name: Barge Min Words
arguments.description: Defines the number of words that must be input before triggering barge behavior, in a range of `1-99`.

arguments.name: Conscience
arguments.description: Sets the prompt which binds the agent to its purpose.

arguments.name: Convo
arguments.description: Injects pre-existing conversation history into the AI session at startup. This allows you to seed the AI agent with context from a previous conversation or provide example interactions.

arguments.name: Conversation Id
arguments.description: Used by `check_for_input` and `save_conversation` to identify an individual conversation.

arguments.name: Debug Webhook Level
arguments.description: Enables debugging to the set URL. Allowed values from `0` - `1`.

arguments.name: Debug Webhook Url
arguments.description: Each interaction between the AI and end user is posted in real time to the established URL.

arguments.name: Debug
arguments.description: Enables debug mode for the AI session.

arguments.name: Direction
arguments.description: Forces the direction of the call to the assistant. Valid values are `inbound` and `outbound`.

arguments.name: Digit Termiantors
arguments.description: DTMF digit, as a string, to signal the end of input (ex: '#')

arguments.name: Digit Timeout
arguments.description: Time, in ms, at the end of digit input to detect end of input. Allowed values from `250` - `10,000`.

arguments.name: End Of Speech Timeout
arguments.description: Amount of silence, in ms, at the end of an utterance to detect end of speech. Allowed values from `250` - `10,000`.

arguments.name: Enable Inner Dialog
arguments.description: Enables the inner dialog feature for background conversation analysis.

arguments.name: Enable Pause
arguments.description: Enables the pause/resume functionality for the AI agent.

arguments.name: Enable Turn Detection
arguments.description: Enables intelligent turn detection that monitors partial speech transcripts.

arguments.name: Eleven Labs Stability
arguments.description: The stability slider determines how stable the voice is and the randomness between each generation. Lowering this slider introduces a broader emotional range for the voice.

arguments.name: Eleven Labs Similarity
arguments.description: The similarity slider dictates how closely the AI should adhere to the original voice when attempting to replicate it. The higher the similarity, the closer the AI will sound to the original voice.

arguments.name: Energy Level
arguments.description: Amount of energy necessary for bot to hear you (in dB). Allowed values from `0.0` - `100.0`.

arguments.name: Hold Music
arguments.description: A URL for the hold music to play, accepting WAV, mp3, and FreeSWITCH tone_stream.

arguments.name: Hold On Process
arguments.description: Enables hold music during SWAIG processing.

arguments.name: Inactivity Timeout
arguments.description: Amount of time, in ms, to wait before exiting the app due to inactivity. Allowed values from `10,000` - `3,600,000`.

arguments.name: Inner Dialog Model
arguments.description: Specifies the AI model to use for the inner dialog feature.

arguments.name: Inner Dialog Prompt
arguments.description: The system prompt that guides the inner dialog AI's behavior.

arguments.name: Inner Dialog Synced
arguments.description: When enabled, synchronizes the inner dialog with the main conversation flow.

arguments.name: Input Poll Freq
arguments.description:
Check for input function with check_for_input.
Example use case: Feeding an inbound SMS to AI on a voice call, eg., for collecting an email address or other complex information.

arguments.name: Interrupt On Noise
arguments.description: When enabled, barges agent upon any sound interruption longer than 1 second.

arguments.name: Interrupt Prompt
arguments.description: Provide a prompt for the agent to handle crosstalk.

arguments.name: Local Tz
arguments.description: The local timezone setting for the AI. Value should use `IANA TZ ID`

arguments.name: Max Response Tokens
arguments.description: Sets the maximum number of tokens the AI model can generate in a single response.

arguments.name: Outbound Attention Timeout
arguments.description: Sets a time duration for the outbound call recipient to respond to the AI agent before timeout, in a range from `10000` to `600000`.

arguments.name: Persist Global Data
arguments.description: When enabled, global_data persists across multiple AI agent invocations within the same call.

arguments.name: Pom Format
arguments.description: Specifies the output format for structured prompts. Valid values are `markdown` or `xml`.

arguments.name: Save Conversation
arguments.description:
Send a summary of the conversation after the call ends.
This requires a `post_url` to be set in the ai parameters and the `conversation_id` defined below.
This eliminates the need for a `post_prompt` in the ai parameters.

arguments.name: Speak When Spoken To
arguments.description: When enabled, the AI agent remains silent until directly addressed by name.

arguments.name: Start Paused
arguments.description: When enabled, the AI agent starts in a paused state.

arguments.name: Swaig Allow Settings
arguments.description: Allows tweaking any of the indicated settings, such as `barge_match_string`, using the returned SWML from the SWAIG function.

arguments.name: Swaig Allow Swml
arguments.description: Allows your SWAIG to return SWML to be executed.

arguments.name: Swaig Post Conversation
arguments.description: Post entire conversation to any SWAIG call.

arguments.name: Swaig Post Swml Vars
arguments.description: Controls whether SWML variables are included in SWAIG function webhook payloads.

arguments.name: Transfer Summary
arguments.description: Pass a summary of a conversation from one AI agent to another. For example, transfer a call summary between support agents in two departments.

arguments.name: Turn Detection Timeout
arguments.description: Time in milliseconds to wait after detecting a potential end-of-turn before finalizing speech recognition.

arguments.name: Vad Config
arguments.description: Configures Silero Voice Activity Detection (VAD) settings. Format: `threshold` or `threshold:frame_ms`. The threshold (0-100) sets sensitivity for detecting voice activity. The optional frame_ms (16-40) sets frame duration in milliseconds.

arguments.description: When false, AI agent will initialize dialogue after call is setup. When true, agent will wait for the user to speak first.

arguments.name: Call Handler
arguments.description:
Specify how the SIP endpoint will handle outbound calls.
- **default**: The SIP endpoint will pull the outbound policy setting from the [SIP Profile Settings](https://my.signalwire.com?page=sip_profile/edit). This allows centralized management of outbound call behavior across multiple endpoints from a single configuration.
- **passthrough**: The SIP endpoint will be allowed to dial PSTN numbers. This permits outbound calling to traditional phone numbers without restrictions.
- **block-pstn**: The SIP endpoint will be blocked from dialing PSTN numbers. Use this to restrict the endpoint from initiating calls to the public telephone network.
- **resource**: Outbound calls from this SIP endpoint will dial the specified resource and execute its instructions. Requires setting `calling_handler_resource_id` to a valid resource. This enables custom call handling workflows for outbound calls. See the [Fabric REST API](/rest/signalwire-rest/endpoints/fabric) for valid resource types.

authentication.description: Use your SignalZen API Secret key for bearer-authenticated backend API access.

setupGuide.title: Connect SignalZen API Secret
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the SignalZen website whose backend data you want to read. This guide uses the API Secret documented in SignalZen's backend API docs.

steps.title: Sign in to your SignalZen Console
steps.description: Open your SignalZen account for the website you want to connect and go to the website settings area.

steps.title: Open the Integration (General) page for that website
steps.description: SignalZen's API docs say the API Secret key is available on the Integration (General) page of your website.

steps.title: Copy the API Secret
steps.description: Copy the API Secret exactly as shown. This is the value used in the Authorization bearer header for backend API requests.

steps.title: Paste the API Secret into the MindCloud connection
steps.description: Use the API Secret as the only backend credential for this wrapper. Keep the public token out of this connection because it is not part of the backend API auth contract.

name: SigParser
description: Extract contacts, companies, and relationship data from email activity

setupGuide.title: Connect SigParser
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a SigParser account with access to the Developers page and an API key.

steps.title: Sign in to SigParser
steps.description: Open SigParser and sign in with the account you want to connect.

steps.title: Open the Developers page
steps.description: In SigParser, go to Settings and then Developers.

steps.title: Create or copy an API key
steps.description: Create a new API key if you do not already have one, or copy an existing API key you want to use for MindCloud.

steps.title: Paste the API key into MindCloud
steps.description: In the MindCloud connection form, paste the API key into the API Key field and save the connection.

name: SimFin
description: Access SimFin bulk financial datasets, including company metadata, fundamentals, derived ratios, share prices, industries, and markets.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: SimFin API key used in the Authorization header with the provider-required api-key prefix.
authentication.notes: SimFin bulk-download requests require the API key as an Authorization header value prefixed with `api-key`. The app stores one API key credential and injects it into the provider-specific header template at request time.

authentication.name: Basic
authentication.description: Authenticate to the SimpleKPI API with your SimpleKPI login email as the Basic auth username, your API token as the Basic auth password, and your tenant subdomain.

credentials.name: Subdomain
credentials.description: Your SimpleKPI tenant subdomain (for https://<subdomain>.simplekpi.com).

setupGuide.title: Connect SimpleKPI API
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need your SimpleKPI tenant subdomain, the email address for a user with API access, and that user’s API token.

steps.title: Find your tenant subdomain
steps.description: Your subdomain is the part before .simplekpi.com in your SimpleKPI URL.

steps.title: Create or copy an API token
steps.description: In SimpleKPI, open your profile or developer settings and copy the API token for the account you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Enter credentials in MindCloud
steps.description: Set Subdomain to your tenant slug. In the Basic auth fields, use your SimpleKPI login email as username and the API token as password.

setupGuide.title: Set up Simpro OAuth 2.0
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: A Simpro administrator must request API access inside the Simpro build you want to connect. If you are not an administrator, ask yours to complete the application request and give you the Client ID and Client Secret.

steps.title: Enter your Simpro build URL
steps.description: In Build URL, enter the full address you use to sign in to Simpro, including https://, for example https://yourcompany.simprosuite.com. Do not enter only your company or build name.

steps.title: Request API access
steps.description: In Simpro, go to System > Setup. Near the bottom, open API, select Applications, and choose Request Access. If API is not available, ask a Simpro administrator to complete these steps.

steps.title: Use the exact redirect URL
steps.description: When Simpro asks for the redirect URL, paste the callback URL exactly as shown here. The connection cannot complete if this value is different.

steps.title: Copy the credentials when Simpro shows them
steps.description: After the application is approved, Simpro issues a Client ID and Client Secret for this build. Paste them into Client ID and Client Secret in the connection form. Simpro shows the Client Secret only at this time, so copy it before leaving the page.

steps.title: Connect Simpro
steps.description: Return to the connection form, confirm Build URL, Client ID, and Client Secret are filled in, then start the connection and approve access in Simpro.

arguments.name: Unique Identifier Columns
arguments.description:
Comma-separated list of columns to use as unique identifiers to find duplicates. Valid values: email, phone, linkedin_url, company_firstname_lastname. Defaults to "email" if not provided (backward compatible with existing behavior).
Note: The order in which you specify columns does not matter. The system will always check for duplicates in this priority order: email, linkedin_url, phone, company_firstname_lastname.
Examples:
  - "email" - Use only email to find duplicates (default)
  - "phone" - Use only phone to find duplicates
  - "linkedin_url" - Use only LinkedIn URL to find duplicates
  - "email,phone" - Use both email and phone to find duplicates
  - "email,phone,linkedin_url,company_firstname_lastname" - Use all four columns

arguments.name: Prospects

name: SmartSurvey
description: SmartSurvey API provides access to survey data, from listing all surveys to getting all the responses for a survey.

authentication.name: Basic
authentication.description: Use your SmartSurvey API Key as the username and your API Key Secret as the password.

setupGuide.title: Connect SmartSurvey
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a SmartSurvey account with API access enabled and a valid API Token plus Token Secret.

steps.title: Sign in to SmartSurvey
steps.description: Log in to the SmartSurvey account that owns the surveys you want MindCloud to access.

steps.title: Open the API Keys area
steps.description: In SmartSurvey, click My Account, then click API Keys.

steps.title: Request API access if needed
steps.description: If API access is not already enabled for your account, click Request API Access, and if prompted click request key.

steps.title: Create a new API key
steps.description: Click Add New API Key. When the new key appears, copy both the API Token and the Token Secret.

steps.title: Enter your SmartSurvey credentials in MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the API Token into the Username field and paste the Token Secret into the Password field when creating the connection.

actions.name: Close Survey

setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a smsmode REST API key with access to the organisation, channel, SMS, RCS, and management resources you plan to use.

steps.title: Open smsmode credentials
steps.description: In smsmode, open the developer or credential settings for your organisation. The smsmode REST docs identify API keys as the credential used for the X-Api-Key request header.

steps.title: Create or copy an API key
steps.description: Create an API key, or copy an existing one, with the roles required for the resources you want MindCloud to access.

steps.title: Paste the key into MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the API key into the API Key field for this connection.

name: Snapchat Lead Generation
description: Create and manage Snapchat lead generation forms, webhook integrations, lead generation creatives, and lead generation ads through the Snapchat Marketing API.

authentication.name: OAuth2
authentication.description: Authenticate with a Snapchat Marketing API OAuth app and authorize MindCloud to act on behalf of a Snapchat business user.
authentication.notes: Snapchat Marketing API uses OAuth2 authorization code flow. Access tokens expire after 3600 seconds and Snapchat documents refresh-token support for renewing access.

setupGuide.title: Connect Snapchat Marketing API
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need to be an Organization Admin in Snap Business Manager and you need a Snapchat OAuth app created for the Marketing API.

steps.title: Open Snap Business Manager
steps.description: Sign in to Snap Business Manager as an Organization Admin.

steps.title: Create or open your OAuth app
steps.description: Go to the Business Details section, create an OAuth app if needed, and make sure the redirect URI is set to the MindCloud callback URL.

steps.title: Confirm the redirect URI
steps.description: Use this exact redirect URI on the Snapchat OAuth app: https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/snapchatLeadGeneration/callback

steps.title: Authorize the connection in MindCloud
steps.description: Return to MindCloud and continue the OAuth popup so Snapchat can issue an access token and refresh token for this connection.

name: Snappy
description: Snappy is a corporate gifting platform for sending gift collections, swag, and experiences to employees, customers, and prospects.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Authenticate with a Snappy company API key sent in the X-Api-Key header.
authentication.notes: Create the first API key in Snappy at Company Settings -> Sharing & Access. Snappy shows the key only once when it is generated.

setupGuide.title: Create a Snappy API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the Snappy company dashboard for the workspace that will own the integration.

steps.title: Sign in to Snappy
steps.description: Open the Snappy login page and sign in to the company account that should own this connection.

steps.title: Open Sharing & Access
steps.description: From the Snappy dashboard, navigate to Company Settings, then open Sharing & Access.

steps.title: Enable API access
steps.description: Turn on API access for your organization if it is not already enabled.

steps.title: Generate a company API key

name: Softr
description: Build portals, internal tools, dashboards, and business apps without code.

credentials.name: Softr Domain

setupGuide.title: Set up your Softr API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need to be the Softr app owner or a workspace collaborator to make API calls. Softr API keys are scoped to one or more workspaces. If you plan to use Softr user-management actions, also have your published app or custom domain ready for the optional Softr Domain field in MindCloud.

steps.title: Open your Softr API settings
steps.description: Sign in to Softr, open the Dashboard, then click your profile icon and go to My account > API Settings.

steps.title: Generate or copy your API key
steps.description: If you do not have a key yet, click Generate API key. Then copy the full key exactly as Softr shows it and keep it confidential.

steps.title: Paste the key into MindCloud
steps.description: Return to the MindCloud connection form and paste the copied value into the Softr API key field.

steps.title: Add your Softr domain when needed
steps.description: If you plan to use Softr user-management actions, enter your published app domain or custom domain in the optional Softr Domain field.

name: SourceGeek for LinkedIn
description: Search, enrich, and message LinkedIn prospects with SourceGeek

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Connect with a SourceGeek API key from Settings > Integrations.

setupGuide.title: Connect SourceGeek with an API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a SourceGeek account connected to your LinkedIn session before you can generate an API key.

steps.title: Create or sign in to your SourceGeek account
steps.description: Open the SourceGeek app and continue with LinkedIn to access your workspace.

steps.title: Connect your LinkedIn session with the SourceGeek browser extension
steps.description: Install the SourceGeek browser extension, keep your LinkedIn session open in the same browser, and click Refresh session in the extension.
breadcrumb: Connect your SourceGeek account to LinkedIn

steps.title: Open the Integrations settings
steps.description: In SourceGeek, go to the Integrations page where n8n connections are managed.

steps.title: Generate an n8n API key
steps.description: Click Add Integration, choose the n8n integration, then click Configure to generate the API key.

steps.title: Paste the API key into this connection
steps.description: Copy the API key from SourceGeek and paste it into the API Key field in MindCloud when creating the connection.

name: Sourcegraph
description: Search, navigate, and analyze code across repositories

authentication.name: Access Token
authentication.description: Use a Sourcegraph access token.

setupGuide.title: Create a Sourcegraph access token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Sign in to Sourcegraph. You need permission to create access tokens for your account.

steps.title: Open your account settings
steps.description: From any Sourcegraph page, click your avatar in the top-right corner and select Settings.

steps.title: Open Access tokens
steps.description: In the left sidebar, select Access tokens.

steps.title: Generate a new token
steps.description: Click Generate new token.

steps.title: Choose the token settings
steps.description: Enter a description, keep the user:all scope selected, and choose an expiration that matches your security policy.

steps.title: Copy the token into MindCloud
steps.description: Click Generate token, then copy the new token immediately and paste it into the MindCloud connection.

description: Upload audio, video, or text to Speak Ai, retrieve transcripts and insights, manage folders and recorders, and export analyzed content.

credentials.description: Temporary Speak Ai session access token returned by the Request Access Token action. Leave blank until you mint one.

setupGuide.title: Connect Speak Ai

steps.title: Copy your API key
steps.description: Copy an existing API key or create a new one on the API Keys page.

steps.title: Paste the API key into MindCloud
steps.description: Return to MindCloud and paste the API key into the connection form.

steps.title: Mint a session token
steps.description: Run the Request Access Token action to generate a temporary access token and refresh token for this Speak Ai account.

steps.title: Paste the returned access token
steps.description: Save the returned access token in the connection before running normal Speak Ai actions. Refresh token storage is optional for now.

name: Sprinklr
description: Sprinklr is an AI-native customer experience platform. This wrapper provides OAuth-authenticated access to Sprinklr API 2.0 resources including search, standard entities, custom entities, accounts, tasks, cases, profiles, messages, and comments.

authentication.name: OAuth 2.0
authentication.description: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow for Sprinklr API 2.0 using the customer code-grant path.
authentication.notes: You need the `Generate Token` permission in Sprinklr to complete OAuth. Sprinklr’s `client_id` must be the API key/app key from the developer portal, not a portal app UUID. Enter the tenant root as API Base URL, for example `https://api3.sprinklr.com/prod4`, and do not include `/api/v2`. Sprinklr documents that only one active token can exist per API key at a time, and refresh tokens are single-use.

credentials.name: API Base URL
credentials.description: Enter the tenant root URL used for OAuth and API calls, for example https://api3.sprinklr.com/prod4 or https://api3.sprinklr.com. Do not include /api/v2 in this value.

setupGuide.title: Connect your Sprinklr account
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Sprinklr user who can generate tokens, plus the API base URL for your tenant.

steps.title: Find your tenant API base URL
steps.description: Log in to the Sprinklr UI, open View Page Source, search for `sentry-environment`, and use it to build the base URL in the format `https://api3.sprinklr.com/<environment>` or `https://api3.sprinklr.com` for the standard production environment.

steps.title: Confirm your user can generate tokens
steps.description: Sprinklr’s OAuth docs require the `Generate Token` permission for the user who completes the browser authorization.

steps.title: Enter the API Base URL in the connection form
steps.description: Use the value you determined for your tenant, for example `https://api3.sprinklr.com/prod4`.

steps.title: Click Connect and sign in to Sprinklr
steps.description: Authorize the app in the browser. If this is your first login, Sprinklr notes you may need to reset your password before continuing.

name: 88stacks Image Generator
description: Generate images and train image generation models with the 88stacks API.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Connect to the 88stacks API with your personal API key from your 88stacks account.

setupGuide.title: Connect your 88stacks API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an active 88stacks account and access to the API key section for your account.

steps.title: Sign in to your 88stacks account
steps.description: Open 88stacks in your browser and sign in with the account that owns the API access you want to use.

steps.title: Open the API key instructions
steps.description: Go to the official 88stacks FAQ and find the section about getting your API key. Follow the link in that section to open the API key page for your account.

steps.title: Create or copy your API key
steps.description: Generate a new API key if needed, then copy the key value so you can paste it into MindCloud.

steps.title: Paste the API key into MindCloud
steps.description: Return to MindCloud, open the 88stacks connection, and paste the API key into the API Key field.

name: Starburst Galaxy
description: Starburst Galaxy is a fully managed data lakehouse and analytics platform built on Trino. This wrapper exposes the Starburst Galaxy Public API for clusters, users, roles, catalogs, tags, service accounts, data products, and data quality summaries.

authentication.name: OAuth2 client credentials
authentication.description: Starburst Galaxy API authentication token using OAuth2 client credentials.
authentication.notes: Starburst Galaxy uses API authentication tokens with OAuth2 client credentials. The token endpoint is account-specific and tokens expire after 10 minutes. Runtime verification is blocked until a valid Secret key is provided.

setupGuide.title: Connect Starburst Galaxy
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Starburst Galaxy role that can manage API authentication tokens. Starburst only shows the Secret key when the token is created.

steps.title: Open API auth token
steps.description: In Starburst Galaxy, go to Access, then API auth token.

steps.title: Generate a token
steps.description: Use Generate new token, enter a clear description, choose the role that should control this connection's API privileges, then create the token.

steps.title: Save the token values
steps.description: Copy the Client ID and Secret key. The Secret key is shown only once.

steps.title: Enter the connection fields
steps.description: Paste the Client ID and Secret key into the MindCloud connection. The token's assigned Starburst role determines which actions can run.

actions.description: Creates and sends a new sign request in Stiply.

arguments.name: Title
arguments.description: The title of the sign request.

arguments.name: Subject
arguments.description: The subject of the e-mail to the signers.

arguments.name: Message
arguments.description:
The message to be included in the e-mail to the signers. The message can have some basic HTML tags. The tags `
`, ``, ``, ``, ``, ``, ``, `
    `, `
      `, `
    1. `, `

      `, `` are allowed. Always use `
      ` for newlines.

arguments.name: Signing Sequence Type
arguments.description: Choose if all signers can sign in parallel or sequential.

arguments.name: Term
arguments.description:
2 digit code representing the sign term (1d = one day, 2w = two weeks, 3m = three months).
When omitted, the account's configured default term will be used.

arguments.name: External Key
arguments.description:
A key for your internal use so you don't have to save the Stiply sign request key in your local database.
However, your external key has to be unique.

arguments.name: Call Back URL
arguments.description:
An URL to be called by Stiply when the last signer has signed the document.
Please note that `key={sign_request_key}`,`external_key={external_key}` and `sign_request_id={sign_request_id}`
shall be added to the call back url querystring.
The URL will be called using a `GET` request.
When the callback responses with an error status code,
the callback is retried 12 times using an exponential backoff algoritm.

arguments.name: Background Color Fields
arguments.description:
A background color for the fields that will be added to the documents.

Currently the following values are supported:

- null: transparent background (default)
- #ffffff: white background

arguments.name: Account ID
arguments.description:
The id of the account to create the sign request in.
The user must have permissions in the provided account.

When left empty, the default account of the user is used.

arguments.name: Role
arguments.description:
A signer can have different roles.
Role is optional, but when provided can have the following values: ‘signer’, ‘approver’, ‘cc’, ‘dc’.
When role is not provided the ‘signer’ role is used as default.
When the value ‘signer’ is set, the signer will need to sign the document regularly.
When the value ‘approver’ is set, the signer will need to approve the document without signing it.
The approver role is only allowed when the signrequest has ‘signing_sequence_type’ set on ‘sequential’.
When the value cc is set, the signer will be notified about the progress of
the sign request and receive a copy of the signed documents.
When the value dc is set, the signer will only receive the signed documents.

arguments.name: Allow Add Fields
arguments.description:
When true, the signer is allowed to add signature fields by clicking on the document.
Please note that the sender is not required to add a signature field to the document
when the signer is allowed to add fields. Can only be used in combination with role signer.

arguments.name: Auth Method
arguments.description:
Authentication method for signer.

- `sms`: signer is identified by sending a SMS with a code to a phone number
- `idin`: signer is identified by using the trusted login method of a Dutch bank (receiving initials, surname, date of birth)
- `idincomplete`: same as idin, but receiving additional data if available (gender, address, email address, phone number)
- `emandate`: signer is requested to provide an electronic payment mandate using a Dutch bank account

When not provided, no identification of the signer will occur.

arguments.name: Invitation Method
arguments.description:
By default Stiply sends an email to the signer with a link to sign the sign request.
If you would like to invite the signer yourself, you should set the invitation_method to `custom`.
In that case Stiply shall not send an email with the sign request to the signer.

After sending the sign request use the
[Get signers of the sign request](#tag/sign-requests/operation/GetSignRequestSigners) endpoint
to get the sign requests's signers with sign link.

Use the value `self` for the first signer to use the Stiply 'self signing' feature.
For more information on the 'self signing' feature, see our
[article in the help center](https://help.stiply.com/nl/articles/260223-self-signing-zelf-ondertekenen-zonder-het-ondertekenproces-te-doorlopen).

arguments.description:
An URL to be called by Stiply when the last signer has signed the document.
Please note that `key={sign_request_key}`,`external_key={external_key}` and `sign_request_id={sign_request_id}`
shall be added to the call back url querystring.
The URL will be called using a `GET` request.
When the callback responses with an error status code,
the callback is retried 12 times using an exponential backoff algoritm.

arguments.description:
The id of the account to create the sign request in.
The user must have permissions in the provided account.

When left empty, the default account of the user is used.

arguments.name: Role
arguments.description:
A signer can have different roles.
Role is optional, but when provided can have the following values: ‘signer’, ‘approver’, ‘cc’, ‘dc’.
When role is not provided the ‘signer’ role is used as default.
When the value ‘signer’ is set, the signer will need to sign the document regularly.
When the value ‘approver’ is set, the signer will need to approve the document without signing it.
The approver role is only allowed when the signrequest has ‘signing_sequence_type’ set on ‘sequential’.
When the value cc is set, the signer will be notified about the progress of
the sign request and receive a copy of the signed documents.
When the value dc is set, the signer will only receive the signed documents.

arguments.name: Allow Add Fields
arguments.description:
When true, the signer is allowed to add signature fields by clicking on the document.
Please note that the sender is not required to add a signature field to the document
when the signer is allowed to add fields. Can only be used in combination with role signer.

arguments.name: Auth Method
arguments.description:

- `idin`: signer is identified by using the trusted login method of a Dutch bank (receiving initials, surname, date of birth)
- `idincomplete`: same as idin, but receiving additional data if available (gender, address, email address, phone number)
- `emandate`: signer is requested to provide an electronic payment mandate using a Dutch bank account

When not provided, no identification of the signer will occur.

arguments.name: Invitation Method

If you would like to invite the signer yourself, you should set the invitation_method to `custom`.
In that case Stiply shall not send an email with the sign request to the signer.

After sending the sign request use the

to get the sign requests's signers with sign link.

steps.title: Use the Docker host-gateway address in MindCloud

name: Stripe
description: Accept payments, manage subscriptions, invoice customers, and reconcile revenue.

authentication.name: Basic
authentication.notes: Place your Stripe API key in the `User` field, keep `Password` blank

setupGuide.title: Set up your Stripe live secret key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the Stripe Developers Dashboard for the account MindCloud should use. Stripe secret keys are server-side credentials and must be kept private.

steps.title: Open the Stripe API keys page
steps.description: In Stripe, open the Developers Dashboard and go to the API keys page. If you cannot view API keys, ask the Stripe account owner to grant you the required team permissions.

steps.title: Switch to live mode
steps.description: Turn off Test mode in the top-right corner so the page shows your live mode keys.

steps.title: Reveal or create a live secret key
steps.description: Use the live mode secret key for this connection. If you need a new one, click Create secret key, complete Stripe's verification step, name the key, and copy the value when Stripe shows it.

steps.title: Paste the key into MindCloud
steps.description: Enter the Stripe secret key as the basic-auth username or API key value in MindCloud. Leave the password blank.

name: Sumsub
description: Digital identity verification and compliance platform for KYC, AML screening, fraud prevention, transaction monitoring, and business verification.

authentication.name: App token + secret key
authentication.description: Authenticate Sumsub API requests with an app token and a secret key. Requests must be signed per request using Sumsub's HMAC header contract.
authentication.notes: Sumsub requests require `X-App-Token`, `X-App-Access-Ts`, and `X-App-Access-Sig`. Compute `X-App-Access-Sig` as a lowercase hex sha256 HMAC over `timestamp + HTTP_METHOD + requestPathWithQuery + requestBodyIfPresent`, using the secret key created with the app token. The timestamp must be within 1 minute of Sumsub server time. Stage 1 stores the credential fields and docs only; runtime request signing still needs to be wired before calls will succeed. The Linear ticket recorded a `401 Unauthorized` with `app-token-signature-mismatch` while validating `/resources/applicants/-/levels`, so the signing implementation must match Sumsub's contract exactly.

name: Survicate
description: Access Survicate Data Export API surveys, responses, respondents, and personal-data endpoints from MindCloud.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Authenticate to Survicate Data Export API with the API key from Surveys Settings -> Access Keys.
authentication.notes: Use the Survicate Data Export API key from the panel's Surveys Settings -> Access Keys area. The API expects it in the `Authorization` header as `Basic {{apiKey}}`.

setupGuide.title: Connect Survicate API Key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Survicate account and a plan with Data Export API access.

steps.title: Open Survicate access keys
steps.description: In Survicate, open Surveys Settings, then Access Keys, and copy your Data Export API key.

steps.title: Paste the API key into MindCloud
steps.description: Enter the copied API key in the connection form. MindCloud will send it as `Authorization: Basic {{apiKey}}` to Survicate Data Export API.

steps.title: Save the connection
steps.description: After saving, you can run survey, response, respondent, and personal-data actions from Cirra or workflows.

setupGuide.title: Set up your Systeme.io Public API key

steps.title: Open your Systeme.io settings
steps.description: In Systeme.io, click your profile picture in the top-right corner and open Settings.

steps.title: Create a Public API key
steps.description: Scroll to the Public API keys section and click Create a key.

steps.title: Name the key and choose an expiration
steps.description: Enter a name that helps you recognize the MindCloud connection later. Optionally set an expiration date, then create the key.

steps.title: Copy the key into MindCloud
steps.description: Copy the generated Public API key and paste it into the MindCloud Systeme.io connection as the API Key value.
